cards.front: Recall a key point about Stimulus & Starting Points
cards.back: A stimulus is the starting point or inspiration for creating a dance

cards.front: Recall a key point about Stimulus & Starting Points
cards.back: There are five main types of stimulus: visual, auditory, kinaesthetic, ideational and literary

cards.front: Recall a key point about Stimulus & Starting Points
cards.back: A visual stimulus is something you see — a painting, photograph, sculpture or film

cards.front: Recall a key point about Stimulus & Starting Points
cards.back: An auditory stimulus is something you hear — music, natural sounds, spoken word or silence

cards.front: Recall a key point about Stimulus & Starting Points
cards.back: A kinaesthetic stimulus comes from physical sensation — a gesture, body action or quality of movement

cards.front: Recall a key point about Stimulus & Starting Points
cards.back: An ideational stimulus is a concept or theme — an emotion, issue, memory or philosophical idea

cards.front: Recall a key point about Stimulus & Starting Points
cards.back: A literary stimulus comes from words — a poem, story, newspaper article or quote

cards.front: Recall a key point about Stimulus & Starting Points
cards.back: One stimulus can inspire movement in many different ways depending on the choreographer

cards.front: Recall a key point about Stimulus & Starting Points
cards.back: Choreographers may combine more than one type of stimulus to enrich their work

cards.front: Recall a key point about Stimulus & Starting Points
cards.back: The choice of stimulus influences the mood, style and content of the final dance

cards.front: Recall a key point about Stimulus & Starting Points
cards.back: In AQA 8236 NEA, you must clearly identify and describe your chosen stimulus

cards.front: Recall a key point about Stimulus & Starting Points
cards.back: Understanding different stimulus types helps you analyse professional works in the written exam
